# autoSpectra

> **Soil spectral modeling, visualization, and prediction** — powered by
> the Open Soil Spectral Library (OSSL v1.2) and soilVAE asymmetric
> autoencoders. Two sensor-agnostic models cover the complete VisNIR and
> MIR spectral ranges with data from any field or laboratory instrument.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Overview

**autoSpectra** is an R package and interactive Shiny application for
predicting soil physical and chemical properties from diffuse
reflectance spectra. It provides **four OSSL-trained model families** —
two algorithms × two spectral domains — so the user can pick between a
sensor-agnostic deep-learning model and a faithful replication of the
[Safanelli et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0296545)
reference Cubist+PCA pipeline:

| Model family | Algorithm | Range | Bands | Sensor-agnostic? |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **OSSL_VisNIR** | masked soilVAE | 350–2500 nm | 1 076 @ 2 nm | yes (any band coverage) |
| **OSSL_MIR** | masked soilVAE | 600–4000 cm⁻¹ | 1 701 @ 2 cm⁻¹ | yes (any band coverage) |
| **OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist** | Cubist + PCA(120) + SNV | 350–2500 nm | 1 076 @ 2 nm | requires full coverage |
| **OSSL_MIR_Cubist** | Cubist + PCA(120) + SNV | 600–4000 cm⁻¹ | 1 701 @ 2 cm⁻¹ | requires full coverage |

All four families were trained on the full [Open Soil Spectral Library
v1.2](https://docs.soilspectroscopy.org) using the same SNV
preprocessing and the same 10-fold cross-validation strategy described
in Safanelli (2025), so the soilVAE numbers are directly comparable to
the Cubist baseline.

> **Why two families?** The **Cubist** baseline reproduces the published
> OSSL methodology — the “ground truth” from the literature. The
> **masked soilVAE** is our contribution: it accepts spectra from any
> instrument, including those that only cover a sub-range (e.g.,
> NeoSpectra 1350–2550 nm), via a binary coverage mask channel and
> `spectral_dropout` augmentation at training time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Models

### OSSL_VisNIR — masked soilVAE (sensor-agnostic, 350–2500 nm)

    Family ID  : OSSL_VisNIR
    Algorithm  : masked Variational Autoencoder, latent dim = 16
    Domain     : Visible + Near-Infrared reflectance
    Grid       : 350 – 2500 nm at 2 nm (1 076 bands)
    Input      : [SNV-spectrum | binary mask]   shape = 2 * 1076
    Pipeline   : -ln(R) -> SG smooth(11,2) -> SNV (per-mask)
    Augmentation: spectral_dropout - 3 simulated cut-offs per training sample
                  (full ASD / 1000 nm Bruker / 1350 nm NeoSpectra)
    Validation : 10-fold CV with refitting (Safanelli 2025)
    AD         : Mahalanobis distance in 16-D latent space (chi-squared at alpha=0.05)

### OSSL_MIR — masked soilVAE (sensor-agnostic, 600–4000 cm⁻¹)

    Family ID  : OSSL_MIR
    Algorithm  : masked Variational Autoencoder, latent dim = 16
    Domain     : Mid-Infrared absorbance (ATR, DRIFTS)
    Grid       : 600 - 4000 cm-1 at 2 cm-1 (1 701 bands)
    Input      : [SNV-spectrum | binary mask]   shape = 2 * 1701
    Pipeline   : SG smooth(11,2) -> SNV (per-mask)
    Validation : 10-fold CV with refitting (Safanelli 2025)
    AD         : Mahalanobis distance in 16-D latent space

### OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist / OSSL_MIR_Cubist — Safanelli 2025 replication

    Algorithm  : Cubist (committees in {1, 5, 10, 15, 20})
    Predictors : First 120 principal components (Safanelli, p. 9)
    Preprocess : SNV (Safanelli ring-trial selection, p. 9)
    Tuning     : 5-fold inner CV on a 2 000-sample subset (Safanelli, p. 9)
    Validation : 10-fold outer CV with refitting (Safanelli, p. 10)
    Targets    : log1p transform for skewed properties (Safanelli, p. 10)
    AD         : Q-statistic on PCA residuals; UCL_Q via Jackson-Mudholkar 1979
                 at 99% confidence (Safanelli eq. 3)
    Uncertainty: normalised conformal prediction with delta = f(T120) error model
                 at 68% confidence ~ 1 SD (Safanelli eqs. 9-10)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Methodology — what we copied from Safanelli (2025) and what we added

The package implements **every key step** of Safanelli et al. (2025) so
the Cubist family is a direct replication. The masked soilVAE family
then changes only the predictive engine, keeping preprocessing,
validation, applicability domain, and uncertainty as comparable as
possible.

| Step | Safanelli 2025 (Cubist) | autoSpectra Cubist family | autoSpectra soilVAE family |
|----|----|----|----|
| Spectral range | 350–2500 / 600–4000 | same | same |
| Preprocessing | SNV alone | SNV alone | SG smooth(11,2) → masked SNV |
| Predictor | First 120 PCs | First 120 PCs | 16-D VAE latent |
| Algorithm | Cubist (committees ∈ {1, 5, 10, 15, 20}) | same | masked VAE |
| Inner tuning | 5-fold CV, ~2 000 sample subset | same | none (callbacks only) |
| Outer validation | 10-fold CV with refitting | same | same |
| Target transform | log1p (skewed properties) | same | same |
| Applicability domain | Q-statistic + UCL_Q (99%) | same | Mahalanobis on latent (95%) |
| Uncertainty | Normalised conformal, 68% PI | same | absolute conformal q90/q95 |
| **Sensor-agnostic for partial coverage** | **no** (separate NeoSpectra model) | no | **yes** (mask + dropout) |

The masked soilVAE is the **only family that handles instruments that
don’t cover the full range** (NeoSpectra 1350–2550 nm, Bruker MPA
800–2500 nm, etc.) without requiring a separate model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Supported Instruments

Any instrument whose spectral output can be resampled to the canonical
OSSL grid is compatible. autoSpectra resamples automatically via linear
interpolation.

| Family | Partial coverage (e.g. NeoSpectra 1350-2550 nm) |
|----|----|
| `OSSL_VisNIR` (masked VAE) | works — coverage encoded in mask channel |
| `OSSL_MIR` (masked VAE) | works |
| `OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist` (Safanelli) | requires (350–2500 nm) coverage; otherwise predict but with low-AD warning |
| `OSSL_MIR_Cubist` (Safanelli) | requires (600–4000 cm⁻¹) coverage |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Supported Instruments

Any instrument whose spectral output can be resampled to the canonical
OSSL grid is compatible. autoSpectra resamples automatically via linear
interpolation.

### VisNIR instruments in OSSL v1.2

| Instrument                       | Manufacturer              | Range (nm) |
|----------------------------------|---------------------------|------------|
| FieldSpec 3 / 4                  | Malvern Panalytical (ASD) | 350–2500   |
| XDS Rapid Content Analyzer       | Foss                      | 400–2500   |
| MPA FT-NIR                       | Bruker                    | 800–2500   |
| Spectrum One FT-NIR              | PerkinElmer               | 1000–2500  |
| MicroNIR                         | VIAVI Solutions           | 908–1676   |
| Other diffuse-reflectance VisNIR | Various                   | ≥400       |

### MIR instruments in OSSL v1.2

| Instrument             | Manufacturer  | Technique     | Range (cm⁻¹) |
|------------------------|---------------|---------------|--------------|
| ALPHA FTIR             | Bruker        | ATR (diamond) | 400–4000     |
| Tensor 27 FTIR         | Bruker        | DRIFTS        | 400–4000     |
| Spectrum Two FT-MIR    | PerkinElmer   | ATR           | 400–4000     |
| Nicolet iS10 / iS50    | Thermo Fisher | ATR / DRIFTS  | 400–4000     |
| Other FTIR instruments | Various       | ATR / DRIFTS  | ≥600         |

> **Bringing a new instrument?** Resample your spectra to the model grid
> (handled automatically by
> [`predict_soil()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_soil.md)),
> and check the applicability domain score. The Mahalanobis distance
> will tell you whether the instrument’s spectral profile is within the
> training distribution.

## Performance Benchmark — Safanelli (2025) baseline

Safanelli et al. (2025) Tables 4 and 5 report an independent evaluation
of the OSSL Cubist + PCA(120) + SNV models across 20 distinct VisNIR /
MIR instruments. Those figures are the reference baseline for this
package, and are quoted verbatim further down.

**A note on comparing against them.** Their evaluation holds out whole
instruments. Any autoSpectra number produced by a random train/test
split is measured on an easier problem and is not comparable to it,
however favourable it looks. Use the leave-one-dataset-out results for
that comparison.

### autoSpectra v0.4.0 — single random 80/20 split

Full training, 60 epochs, all four families. Metrics are test-set values
in original units (`log1p` targets are back-transformed before scoring).

| Sensor | Property | soilVAE (R² / RMSE / CCC) | Cubist (R² / RMSE / CCC) | Safanelli (R² / RMSE / CCC) |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **VisNIR** | oc | 0.850 / 4.82 / 0.906 | 0.941 / 3.04 / 0.970 | 0.78 / 5.27 / 0.82 |
| **VisNIR** | n.tot | 0.899 / 0.17 / 0.945 | 0.910 / 0.16 / 0.951 | 0.81 / — / — |
| **VisNIR** | ph.h2o | 0.866 / 0.50 / 0.924 | 0.864 / 0.50 / 0.928 | 0.50 / 1.22 / 0.65 |
| **VisNIR** | clay.tot | 0.805 / 6.86 / 0.884 | 0.829 / 6.42 / 0.902 | 0.25 / 13.35 / 0.38 |
| **MIR** | oc | 0.894 / 4.37 / 0.930 | 0.990 / 1.32 / 0.995 | 0.96 / 1.16 / 0.95 |
| **MIR** | n.tot | 0.858 / 0.24 / 0.913 | 0.882 / 0.22 / 0.937 | 0.96 / — / — |
| **MIR** | ph.h2o | 0.917 / 0.38 / 0.954 | 0.909 / 0.40 / 0.951 | 0.75 / 0.72 / 0.84 |
| **MIR** | clay.tot | 0.921 / 4.91 / 0.957 | 0.903 / 5.41 / 0.949 | 0.62 / 8.82 / 0.74 |

> ⚠️ **Do not read the last two columns as a head-to-head, and do not
> read ours as beating the baseline.** The evaluations are not
> equivalent. Ours is a single random 80/20 split of the whole OSSL;
> Safanelli’s is a mean over 20 instruments, each held out in turn. A
> random split leaves samples from the same dataset, region and
> instrument on both sides of the train/test line, which is materially
> easier than predicting a population the model has never seen. MIR `oc`
> Cubist at R² 0.990 sits above what the literature reports for this
> task — a reason for suspicion, not a result to advertise.

### The comparable evaluation: leave-one-dataset-out

Because the protocols differ, the single-split numbers above cannot
answer whether the models generalise. Leave-one-dataset-out
(`--cv10 --lodo`) withholds an entire OSSL contributing dataset per
fold, which is the same kind of test Safanelli reports.

It changes the picture substantially. On VisNIR `oc`, Cubist scores **R²
0.57 under LODO against 0.94 on the random split**: most of the apparent
margin was the evaluation, not the model.

R² is weighted by fold size, because LODO folds are few and very unequal
(one VisNIR fold holds 40,175 samples, another 50). RMSE is pooled
across folds in quadrature. Only the Cubist families have been run under
LODO so far.

**VisNIR — Cubist under LODO (4 held-out datasets)**

| Property   | R²     | RMSE  | CCC   | R² median fold | Safanelli R² / RMSE / CCC |
|------------|--------|-------|-------|----------------|---------------------------|
| `oc`       | 0.569  | 9.40  | 0.784 | 0.531          | 0.78 / 5.27 / 0.82        |
| `n.tot`    | −4.344 | 1.71  | 0.571 | 0.702          | 0.81 / — / —              |
| `ph.h2o`   | 0.478  | 0.99  | 0.725 | −0.442         | 0.50 / 1.22 / 0.65        |
| `clay.tot` | 0.430  | 12.25 | 0.643 | 0.143          | 0.25 / 13.35 / 0.38       |

**MIR — Cubist under LODO (7–8 held-out datasets)**

| Property   | R²    | RMSE  | CCC   | R² median fold | Safanelli R² / RMSE / CCC |
|------------|-------|-------|-------|----------------|---------------------------|
| `oc`       | 0.809 | 5.78  | 0.869 | 0.808          | 0.96 / 1.16 / 0.95        |
| `n.tot`    | 0.677 | 0.36  | 0.792 | 0.538          | 0.96 / — / —              |
| `ph.h2o`   | 0.759 | 0.64  | 0.868 | 0.600          | 0.75 / 0.72 / 0.84        |
| `clay.tot` | 0.127 | 15.70 | 0.593 | 0.254          | 0.62 / 8.82 / 0.74        |

How to read it:

- **This is the comparison that holds up, and it is mixed.** VisNIR
  `clay.tot` and `ph.h2o` are close to or ahead of Safanelli on R², RMSE
  and CCC. Organic carbon and nitrogen are behind on both sensors, and
  MIR `clay.tot` is well behind.
- **VisNIR `n.tot` fails on one fold.** Two of its three folds score R²
  0.70 and 0.90. The third, about 19,800 samples, scores −14.7, and
  because it is a third of the data it drags the weighted R² to −4.3.
  That is a genuine domain shift — a population whose
  nitrogen-to-spectrum relationship the remaining datasets do not cover
  — not a numerical artefact: the bounded back-transform is already in
  place.
- **The median fold is shown because the folds disagree.** Where
  weighted R² and median differ sharply (`n.tot`, `ph.h2o` on VisNIR),
  performance depends heavily on which dataset is held out.
- Safanelli held out instruments and we hold out contributing datasets.
  Both test on unseen populations, but they are not the same partition,
  so treat close values as comparable rather than as a ranking.

LODO also exposed a real defect, now fixed: an unbounded
[`expm1()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Log.html) back-transform turned a
handful of out-of-domain overshoots into enormous absolute errors, and
it destroyed exactly the `log1p` properties. Bounding the back-transform
to the calibration range moved the unweighted mean fold R² for VisNIR
`oc` from −1.21 to +0.54, and collapsed the between-fold SD from ±3.76
to ±0.36. Untransformed properties were unaffected, which is what
confirmed the mechanism. See `R/target_transform.R`.

Both tables above are generated from the artefacts — never hand-written
— by:

``` bash
Rscript tools/benchmark_table.R
```

`--check` makes it exit non-zero while any family or property is
missing, so a table cannot be published from a half-finished validation
run.

### VisNIR (Safanelli 2025, Table 4 — Cubist + OSSL, mean over 20 instruments)

| Property                 | RMSE  | bias  | R²   | CCC  | RPIQ |
|--------------------------|-------|-------|------|------|------|
| Organic Carbon (oc)      | 5.27  | -0.88 | 0.78 | 0.82 | 0.65 |
| pH (H₂O)                 | 1.22  | -0.21 | 0.50 | 0.65 | 2.18 |
| Clay total               | 13.35 | -2.40 | 0.25 | 0.38 | 1.35 |
| K extractable (cmolc/kg) | 1.09  | -0.49 | 0.23 | 0.28 | 0.51 |

### MIR (Safanelli 2025, Table 5 — Cubist + OSSL, mean over 20 instruments)

| Property                 | RMSE | bias  | R²   | CCC  | RPIQ |
|--------------------------|------|-------|------|------|------|
| Organic Carbon (oc)      | 1.16 | -0.01 | 0.96 | 0.95 | 2.96 |
| pH (H₂O)                 | 0.72 | 0.11  | 0.75 | 0.84 | 2.92 |
| Clay total               | 8.82 | -1.84 | 0.62 | 0.74 | 1.81 |
| K extractable (cmolc/kg) | 0.44 | -0.07 | 0.49 | 0.61 | 1.48 |

> Aggregate (all properties, 10-fold internal CV — Safanelli 2025,
> p. 17): MIR Cubist + OSSL **mean Lin’s CCC = 0.78, mean RPIQ = 2.11**.

> Per-family per-property metrics for autoSpectra are written
> automatically to: `models/<family_id>/metrics_summary.json`
> (single-split test metrics) `models/<family_id>/cv10_summary.json`
> (10-fold CV mean ± SD) after running `Rscript train_ossl.R [--cv10]`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Architecture

### soilVAE — Asymmetric Autoencoder

    Input spectrum (d_in preprocessed bands)
            │
            ▼
      ┌──────────────────┐
      │   Dense 256 ReLU │
      │   Dense 128 ReLU │
      │   Dense  64 ReLU │
      │   Dense  16 ReLU │ ← Latent space z  (information bottleneck)
      └────────┬─────────┘
               │
        ┌──────┴──────────────────────┐
        │                             │
        ▼  Reconstruction head        ▼  Prediction head
      Dense 32  ReLU               Dense 64  ReLU
      Dense d_in  linear           Dropout 5%
      ↑ MSE loss (w = 0.3)         Dense 1  linear
      (forces encoder to           ↑ MSE loss (w = 0.3)
       retain spectral info)       (soil property output)

| Hyperparameter          | Value                                      |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Latent dimension        | 16                                         |
| Optimizer               | Adam                                       |
| Max epochs              | 80                                         |
| Early stopping patience | 10 (monitor `val_loss`)                    |
| LR reduction            | ×0.5 at plateau, patience 5, min 1×10⁻⁵    |
| Validation split        | 15% of training set                        |
| Conformal intervals     | q90, q95 of calibration absolute residuals |

### Applicability Domain

    Training latent vectors → (μ, Σ)   [16 × 16 covariance]

    New sample z:
      D²(z) = (z − μ)ᵀ Σ⁻¹ (z − μ)

      D² ≤ χ²(16, 0.95) ≈ 26.3  →  ✓ within domain
      D² > 26.3                  →  ⚠ out of domain (extrapolation warning)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Preprocessing Pipeline

Following Safanelli (2025), SNV is the canonical preprocessing step — it
was selected through the SS4GG ring-trial experiment because it removes
both instrument-specific scaling and particle-size scattering (the two
dominant sources of inter-instrument variation) without sacrificing
predictive accuracy.

                            Cubist family (Safanelli replication)
       VisNIR (reflectance)                        MIR (absorbance)
       --------------------                        ----------------
       Raw reflectance R                           Raw absorbance A
               |                                            |
               v                                            |
       A = -ln(R)                                           |
               |                                            |
               v                                            v
            SNV (per-row)                              SNV (per-row)
               |                                            |
               v                                            v
       PCA (first 120 PCs) - same per family             same
               |                                            |
               v                                            v
       Cubist (committees from inner CV)                 same

The masked soilVAE family additionally Savitzky-Golay smooths the
spectrum before SNV (helps the encoder generalise across noise levels),
and uses a **per-mask SNV** that computes the row mean / SD using only
the bands that the source instrument actually covered:

``` r

# Cubist (Safanelli replication)
preprocess = c("ABSORBANCE", "SNV")          # VisNIR
preprocess = c("SNV")                         # MIR

# Masked soilVAE (sensor-agnostic)
preprocess = c("ABSORBANCE", "SG_SMOOTH(11,2)", "SNV_MASKED")  # VisNIR
preprocess = c("SG_SMOOTH(11,2)", "SNV_MASKED")                # MIR
```

For the masked-VAE family, training-time augmentation
(`spectral_dropout`) generates two extra copies per sample with
randomised low-end cut-offs that mimic real instruments (NeoSpectra @
1350 nm, Bruker MPA @ 800 nm, etc.). The encoder therefore learns a
single representation that handles every realistic coverage pattern.

### OSSL Level-1 Harmonized Properties (34 targets)

| Category           | Variable         | Unit     | Description                   |
|--------------------|------------------|----------|-------------------------------|
| **Organic**        | `oc`             | w.pct    | Organic carbon                |
|                    | `c.tot`          | w.pct    | Total carbon                  |

| **Texture**        | `clay.tot`       | w.pct    | Total clay (\<0.002 mm)       |
|                    | `silt.tot`       | w.pct    | Total silt (0.002–0.05 mm)    |
|                    | `sand.tot`       | w.pct    | Total sand (0.05–2 mm)        |
| **Reaction**       | `ph.h2o`         | index    | pH in water                   |
|                    | `ph.cacl2`       | index    | pH in CaCl₂                   |
|                    | `caco3`          | w.pct    | Calcium carbonate             |
|                    | `acidity`        | cmolc/kg | Exchangeable acidity          |
|                    | `ec`             | dS/m     | Electrical conductivity       |
| **Physical**       | `bd`             | g/cm³    | Bulk density                  |
|                    | `aggstb`         | w.pct    | Aggregate stability           |
|                    | `awc.33.1500kPa` | w.frac   | Available water content       |
|                    | `wr.33kPa`       | w.pct    | Water retention at 33 kPa     |
|                    | `wr.1500kPa`     | w.pct    | Water retention at 1500 kPa   |
| **Exchange**       | `cec`            | cmolc/kg | Cation exchange capacity      |
|                    | `ca.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable calcium           |
|                    | `k.ext`          | mg/kg    | Extractable potassium         |
|                    | `mg.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable magnesium         |
|                    | `na.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable sodium            |
| **Micronutrients** | `p.ext`          | mg/kg    | Extractable phosphorus        |
|                    | `fe.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable iron              |
|                    | `fe.dith`        | w.pct    | Crystalline iron (dithionite) |
|                    | `fe.ox`          | w.pct    | Amorphous iron (oxalate)      |
|                    | `al.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable aluminum          |
|                    | `al.ox`          | w.pct    | Amorphous aluminum            |
|                    | `al.dith`        | w.pct    | Crystalline aluminum          |
|                    | `mn.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable manganese         |
|                    | `zn.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable zinc              |
|                    | `cu.ext`         | mg/kg    | Extractable copper            |
|                    | `b.ext`          | mg/kg    | Extractable boron             |
|                    | `s.tot`          | w.pct    | Total sulfur                  |
|                    | `s.ext`          | mg/kg    | Extractable sulfur            |

## OSSL Data Sources

All OSSL v1.2 data are publicly available under [CC-BY
4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Artifacts distributed from this repository that are **derived from OSSL
v1.2** — the trained models published on Zenodo (record
[19004686](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19004686)) — inherit that
attribution requirement: please cite the OSSL as described in [Data
Citations](#data-citations).

| Component | File | URL |
|----|----|----|
| VisNIR spectra (L0) | `ossl_visnir_L0_v1.2.csv.gz` | `https://storage.googleapis.com/soilspec4gg-public/ossl_visnir_L0_v1.2.csv.gz` |
| MIR spectra (L0) | `ossl_mir_L0_v1.2.csv.gz` | `https://storage.googleapis.com/soilspec4gg-public/ossl_mir_L0_v1.2.csv.gz` |
| Soil lab data (L1) | `ossl_soillab_L1_v1.2.csv.gz` | `https://storage.googleapis.com/soilspec4gg-public/ossl_soillab_L1_v1.2.csv.gz` |

``` r

ossl_download()          # VisNIR + MIR + soillab (~2 GB)
ossl_download("visnir")  # VisNIR only
ossl_download("mir")     # MIR only
```

| OSSL Level | Description                                                   |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **L0**     | Original contributed spectra (used for training)              |
| **L1**     | Harmonized soil lab values in common units (training targets) |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

``` r

# Install devtools if needed
install.packages("devtools")

# Install autoSpectra
devtools::install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/autoSpectra")
```

### Core dependencies

| Package | Role |
|----|----|
| `shiny`, `shinyWidgets` | Interactive interface |
| `ggplot2` | Visualization |
| `prospectr` | Savitzky-Golay filter |
| `keras3` + `tensorflow` | soilVAE training and inference (optional; Cubist families do not need it) |
| `Cubist`, `irlba` | Cubist + PCA families |
| `httr`, `data.table` | OSSL data download and loading |
| `readxl`, `writexl` | Excel I/O |
| `MASS` | Mahalanobis distance (pseudoinverse) |

**Setting up Keras/TensorFlow:**

``` r

install.packages("keras3")
keras3::install_keras()   # installs TensorFlow in a managed virtualenv
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick Start

### 1. Install and download pre-trained models

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/autoSpectra")

library(autoSpectra)

# One-time download from Zenodo (all four families)
download_ossl_models()

# Or pick exactly what you need
download_ossl_models(c("OSSL_VisNIR", "OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist"))   # VisNIR pair
```

> Models are extracted under `models/` (override with
> `options(autoSpectra.model_dir = ...)`). VAE weights are loaded into
> the session cache on first prediction; Cubist bundles are read on
> demand from `<family>/models/<prop>_cubist.rds`.

### 2. Predict from new spectra

``` r

library(autoSpectra)
df <- readxl::read_excel("my_visnir_spectra.xlsx")

# (a) Sensor-agnostic masked VAE - works for any VisNIR coverage
out_vae <- predict_soil(df, "OSSL_VisNIR",
                        properties = c("oc", "clay.tot", "ph.h2o"))

# (b) Safanelli 2025 Cubist baseline - same call, different family
#     Add with_pi = TRUE to also return 68% prediction intervals
out_cubist <- predict_soil(df, "OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist",
                           properties = c("oc", "clay.tot", "ph.h2o"),
                           with_pi    = TRUE)

# Applicability domain (auto-dispatches Q-statistic vs Mahalanobis)
app <- predict_applicability(df, "OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist", "oc")
plot_applicability(app)

# Visualisation
plot_spectra(df, family = get_family("OSSL_VisNIR"))
plot_mean_spectrum(df, family = get_family("OSSL_VisNIR"))
```

### 3. Pre-load (VAE families) for batch prediction

``` r

preload_ossl_models("OSSL_VisNIR")          # caches all VAE weights once
for (f in my_files) {
  df  <- readxl::read_excel(f)
  out <- predict_soil(df, "OSSL_VisNIR")    # reuses in-memory cache
  writexl::write_xlsx(out, sub("\\.xlsx$", "_pred.xlsx", f))
}
```

### 4. Launch the interactive app

``` r

run_autoSpectra()
```

### Advanced: retrain from OSSL source data

``` r

ossl_download()                    # ~2 GB, cached locally
```

``` bash
# Train all four families (GPU recommended for VAE; ~6-10 h on CPU)
Rscript train_ossl.R

# Subsets:
Rscript train_ossl.R --only-vae              # both masked VAEs only
Rscript train_ossl.R --only-cubist           # Safanelli baseline only
Rscript train_ossl.R OSSL_MIR_Cubist         # one family
Rscript train_ossl.R --cv10                  # 10-fold CV with refitting
Rscript train_ossl.R --quick                 # 4 properties, 20 epochs, 3 folds
```

After training, package the outputs for Zenodo upload with:

``` bash
Rscript upload_models.R
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Shiny Interface

The app provides a streamlined four-tab workflow:

| Tab | Description |
|----|----|
| **Preview** | Sample count, detected bands, spectral range overlap check |
| **Spectrum Viewer** | Per-sample spectrum with model grid overlay |
| **Mean Spectrum** | Mean ± SD ribbon across all uploaded samples |
| **Predictions** | Predicted soil properties (table), applicability domain plot, Excel download |

**Model selection** is the first step: choose one of the four families
(VisNIR / MIR × masked soilVAE / Cubist+PCA) from the sidebar. The badge
shows the active algorithm. VAE weights are loaded into memory on first
prediction; Cubist bundles are read on demand. The “Prediction
intervals” checkbox enables Safanelli-style 68% PIs for the Cubist
families.

**Supported upload formats**: `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.csv`

**Expected file format**:

    Soil_ID  | 350  | 352  | 354  | ... | 2500
    ---------|------|------|------|-----|------
    Sample_1 | 0.12 | 0.13 | 0.14 | ... | 0.08
    Sample_2 | 0.18 | 0.19 | 0.20 | ... | 0.11

Column headers must be the wavelength (nm) or wavenumber (cm⁻¹)
positions. The `Soil_ID` column is configurable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Versioning

### v0.4.0 — 2026-04-24 *(current)*

**Safanelli (2025) faithful redesign + masked soilVAE**

- **Four official families**: `OSSL_VisNIR`, `OSSL_MIR` (masked soilVAE)
  and `OSSL_VisNIR_Cubist`, `OSSL_MIR_Cubist` (Safanelli replication)
- **Cubist + PCA(120) + SNV** baseline that exactly replicates the OSSL
  methodology of Safanelli et al. (2025) — same preprocessing, 5-fold
  inner CV committee tuning, log1p target transform, Q-statistic UCL
  applicability domain, normalised conformal prediction at 68% PI
- **Masked soilVAE**: input shape `2 * d_spec` carrying spectrum +
  binary coverage mask; trained with `spectral_dropout` augmentation
  simulating ASD / Bruker MPA / NeoSpectra / PerkinElmer cut-offs — a
  single model handles every realistic instrument
- **Spectral ranges aligned with Safanelli**: VisNIR 350-2500 nm (1 076
  bands), MIR 600-4000 cm⁻¹ (1 701 bands)
- **10-fold CV with refitting** (Safanelli’s outer loop) —
  `Rscript train_ossl.R --cv10` writes per-property `cv10_summary.json`
- **Unified
  [`predict_applicability()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_applicability.md)**:
  dispatches Q-statistic for Cubist or Mahalanobis for VAE, returns the
  same schema (`score`, `threshold`, `in_domain`)
- **Shiny app**: 4-family selector with algorithm badge,
  prediction-interval toggle for Cubist families
- New modules: `R/applicability.R`, `R/conformal.R`,
  `R/cubist_baseline.R`, `R/train_cv.R`

### v0.3.0 — 2026-03-13

**OSSL-only sensor-agnostic redesign**

- **Two official models**: `OSSL_VisNIR` and `OSSL_MIR` — full OSSL v1.2
  training, all instruments
- **Scientific sensor-agnostic methodology**: absorbance/SG-smooth/SNV
  preprocessing + soilVAE information bottleneck + latent applicability
  domain
- **10-fold CV stratified by OSSL dataset**: honest cross-instrument
  performance estimates (mean ± SD)
- **In-memory model cache** (`R/cache.R`):
  [`get_cached_model()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/get_cached_model.md),
  [`preload_ossl_models()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/preload_ossl_models.md)
  — zero-overhead repeated prediction
- **Simplified Shiny UX**: two-model selector, lazy preload,
  applicability domain panel
- `train_ossl.R` rewritten: stratified k-fold CV, per-fold metrics,
  `metrics_summary.json`
- All R CMD check WARNINGs resolved; pkgdown site live
- Zenodo DOI registered: `10.5281/zenodo.19004686`

### v0.2.0 — 2026-03-13

**Major: R package + OSSL integration**

- Converted from standalone Shiny app to a proper R package
- Added OSSL v1.2 data download and integration
- Expanded to 34 OSSL L1 soil properties
- Two-step SG preprocessing (explicit smooth + derivative passes)
- MIR support, applicability domain, visualization functions
- roxygen2 documentation (44 exported functions)

### v0.1.0 — 2025

**Initial release: Shiny application**

- Interactive Shiny app for soil spectral prediction
- 23 soil properties, local training data
- soilVAE asymmetric autoencoder architecture

# Package index

## OSSL Data

Download the Open Soil Spectral Library from its official storage bucket
into a user-local cache. autoSpectra never redistributes OSSL data.

- [`ossl_cache_dir()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_cache_dir.md)
  : Default local cache directory for OSSL data
- [`ossl_download()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_download.md)
  : Download all three OSSL components (VisNIR, MIR, soillab)
- [`ossl_download_file()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_download_file.md)
  : Download one OSSL component file to the cache directory
- [`ossl_join()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_join.md)
  : Join OSSL spectra with soil lab data for model training
- [`ossl_l1_labels`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_l1_labels.md)
  : Fancy display labels for OSSL L1 properties
- [`ossl_l1_log_transform`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_l1_log_transform.md)
  : Properties that Safanelli log1p-transforms before fitting
- [`ossl_l1_properties`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_l1_properties.md)
  : All OSSL Level-1 harmonized soil property variable names (34
  targets)
- [`ossl_load_raw()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_load_raw.md)
  : Load a cached OSSL CSV (gzipped) as a data.table
- [`ossl_mir_instruments`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_mir_instruments.md)
  : MIR instruments contributing to OSSL v1.2
- [`ossl_mir_matrix()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_mir_matrix.md)
  : Extract OSSL MIR spectra as a matrix aligned to the OSSL standard
  grid
- [`ossl_prepare()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_prepare.md)
  : Convenience: load and join all OSSL data for a given sensor type
- [`ossl_soillab()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_soillab.md)
  : Extract OSSL Level-1 soil lab data for a set of properties
- [`ossl_visnir_instruments`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_visnir_instruments.md)
  : VisNIR instruments contributing to OSSL v1.2
- [`ossl_visnir_matrix()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_visnir_matrix.md)
  : Extract OSSL VisNIR spectra as a matrix aligned to the OSSL standard
  grid

## Pre-trained Models

Download the published model families from Zenodo (one-time setup)

- [`download_ossl_models()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/download_ossl_models.md)
  : Download pre-trained OSSL soilVAE models from Zenodo
- [`models_available()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/models_available.md)
  : Check whether pre-trained models are available locally
- [`audit_release_archive()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/audit_release_archive.md)
  : Audit a built release archive for redistributed OSSL training data

## Prediction

Predict soil properties, with intervals and applicability domain

- [`predict_soil()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_soil.md)
  : Predict soil properties from a spectral data frame
- [`predict_applicability()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_applicability.md)
  : Compute applicability-domain scores for new spectra
- [`format_predictions()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/format_predictions.md)
  : Round predictions and rename columns to display labels
- [`get_family()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/get_family.md)
  : Lookup a model family from the registry
- [`family_matches()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/family_matches.md)
  : Test whether a family matches a sensor type
- [`property_label()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/property_label.md)
  : Get a display label for a soil property key

## Preprocessing

Spectral preprocessing, resampling and coverage masks

- [`preprocess_visnir()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/preprocess_visnir.md)
  : Canonical Safanelli preprocessing for VisNIR (reflectance input)
- [`preprocess_mir()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/preprocess_mir.md)
  : Canonical Safanelli preprocessing for MIR (absorbance input)
- [`reflectance_to_absorbance()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/reflectance_to_absorbance.md)
  : Convert reflectance to absorbance
- [`apply_pipeline()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/apply_pipeline.md)
  : Apply a spectral preprocessing pipeline
- [`apply_sg_matrix()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/apply_sg_matrix.md)
  : Apply Savitzky-Golay filter row-wise to a spectral matrix
- [`apply_snv()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/apply_snv.md)
  : Apply Standard Normal Variate (SNV) row-wise
- [`apply_snv_masked()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/apply_snv_masked.md)
  : Apply SNV using only the masked (covered) bands of each row
- [`parse_sg()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/parse_sg.md)
  : Parse SG parameter string of the form "SG(m,p)", "SG(m,p,d)", etc.
- [`sg_safe_params()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/sg_safe_params.md)
  : Compute safe SG parameters given available number of columns
- [`resample_to_grid()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/resample_to_grid.md)
  : Resample a spectral matrix to a target wavelength grid via linear
  interpolation
- [`get_wavelengths()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/get_wavelengths.md)
  : Extract wavelength/wavenumber positions from a data frame's column
  names
- [`mask_from_coverage()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/mask_from_coverage.md)
  : Build a coverage mask from a resampled spectral matrix
- [`has_spectral_coverage()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/has_spectral_coverage.md)
  : Which rows carry any spectral signal at all

## Target Transforms

log1p transform for skewed properties and its bounded inverse, which
keeps predictions inside the calibration range

- [`apply_target_transform()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/apply_target_transform.md)
  : Forward log1p transform for properties whose policy asks for it
- [`invert_target_transform()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/invert_target_transform.md)
  : Invert the target transform without letting it explode
- [`target_bounds()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/target_bounds.md)
  : Training-scale bounds used to keep a back-transform from
  extrapolating
- [`metrics_original_scale()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/metrics_original_scale.md)
  : Score predictions in original units, with the bounded back-transform

## soilVAE Family

Masked, sensor-agnostic variational autoencoder

- [`build_maskedVAE()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/build_maskedVAE.md)
  : Build a masked soilVAE for sensor-agnostic prediction
- [`train_maskedVAE()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/train_maskedVAE.md)
  : Train a masked soilVAE for one soil property
- [`build_soilVAE()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/build_soilVAE.md)
  : Build a standard soilVAE
- [`train_soilVAE()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/train_soilVAE.md)
  : Train a (standard) soilVAE model for one soil property
- [`load_soilVAE()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/load_soilVAE.md)
  : Load a saved soilVAE model and its scaler
- [`spectral_dropout()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/spectral_dropout.md)
  : Random spectral-dropout augmentation for masked-VAE training
- [`train_ossl_models()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/train_ossl_models.md)
  : Train soilVAE models for all properties of one model family using
  OSSL data

## Cubist + PCA Family

Replication of Safanelli et al. (2025)

- [`train_cubist_pca()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/train_cubist_pca.md)
  : Train one Cubist + PCA(120) model for a single soil property
- [`load_cubist_pca()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/load_cubist_pca.md)
  : Load a saved Cubist + PCA bundle for a property
- [`predict_cubist_pca()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_cubist_pca.md)
  : Predict with a Cubist + PCA bundle

## Applicability Domain

Q-statistic (Cubist) and latent-space Mahalanobis distance (soilVAE)

- [`q_statistic()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/q_statistic.md)
  : Compute the Q-statistic for each row of a PCA residual matrix
- [`q_statistic_ucl()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/q_statistic_ucl.md)
  : Upper Confidence Limit for the Q-statistic (Jackson-Mudholkar 1979)
- [`predict_q_statistic()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_q_statistic.md)
  : Compute Q-statistic and in-domain flag for new spectra against a
  fitted PCA
- [`mahalanobis_d2()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/mahalanobis_d2.md)
  : Squared Mahalanobis distance against a multivariate Gaussian (mu,
  Sigma)
- [`mahalanobis_threshold()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/mahalanobis_threshold.md)
  : Chi-squared threshold for the Mahalanobis test in latent space

## Prediction Intervals

Conformal calibration

- [`train_normalized_conformal()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/train_normalized_conformal.md)
  : Train a normalised-conformal calibration for a Cubist + PCA model
- [`predict_with_pi()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/predict_with_pi.md)
  : Predict with prediction intervals using a normalised-conformal
  calibration
- [`absolute_conformal()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/absolute_conformal.md)
  : Simple absolute-residual conformal calibration (used by the VAE
  family)

## Validation

Cross-validation, including leave-one-dataset-out

- [`cv_train_property()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/cv_train_property.md)
  : Perform 10-fold CV with refitting for one (family, property)
  combination
- [`random_kfold()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/random_kfold.md)
  : Build random 10-fold indices (Safanelli default)
- [`stratified_kfold()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/stratified_kfold.md)
  : Build Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) k-fold indices
- [`split_idx()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/split_idx.md)
  : Split indices into train / calibration / test sets
- [`metrics_from_y()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/metrics_from_y.md)
  : Compute prediction metrics (RMSE, Bias, R², RPIQ, CCC)

## In-Memory Model Cache

Load models once per session and reuse them without disk I/O

- [`get_cached_model()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/get_cached_model.md)
  : Retrieve a soilVAE model from the in-memory cache
- [`preload_ossl_models()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/preload_ossl_models.md)
  : Pre-load all soilVAE models for a family into memory
- [`list_cached_models()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/list_cached_models.md)
  : List models currently held in the in-memory cache
- [`clear_model_cache()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/clear_model_cache.md)
  : Clear the in-memory model cache

## Visualization

Plotting functions

- [`plot_spectra()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/plot_spectra.md)
  : Plot one or more spectra from a data frame
- [`plot_mean_spectrum()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/plot_mean_spectrum.md)
  : Plot a mean spectrum with +/-1 SD ribbon
- [`plot_predictions()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/plot_predictions.md)
  : Plot predicted vs observed values for a soil property
- [`plot_applicability()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/plot_applicability.md)
  : Plot applicability-domain scores

## Registry

Model registry and metadata

- [`model_registry`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/model_registry.md)
  : Official autoSpectra model family registry
- [`ossl_l1_properties`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_l1_properties.md)
  : All OSSL Level-1 harmonized soil property variable names (34
  targets)
- [`ossl_l1_labels`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_l1_labels.md)
  : Fancy display labels for OSSL L1 properties
- [`ossl_visnir_instruments`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_visnir_instruments.md)
  : VisNIR instruments contributing to OSSL v1.2
- [`ossl_mir_instruments`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/ossl_mir_instruments.md)
  : MIR instruments contributing to OSSL v1.2

## Shiny App

Launch the interactive application

- [`run_autoSpectra()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/run_autoSpectra.md)
  : Launch the autoSpectra Shiny application

## Utilities

Lower-level helpers used by the trainers

- [`save_scaler()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/save_scaler.md)
  : Save a z-score scaler to RDS and JSON
- [`save_metrics_json()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/save_metrics_json.md)
  : Save per-model metrics JSON (RMSE, R2, RPIQ, conformal quantiles,
  latent stats)
- [`feature_minmax()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/feature_minmax.md)
  : Compute per-band min/max feature range from a preprocessed matrix
- [`dir_create()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/dir_create.md)
  : Create a directory if it does not already exist
- [`vneed()`](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/reference/vneed.md)
  : Safe shiny::validate wrapper

  autoSpectra](https://HugoMachadoRodrigues.github.io/autoSpectra/articles/autoSpectra.md):
